To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we present an algorithm that is based on the Gauss—Jordan method, and is capable of estimating the spectral norm of an inverse matrix in a number of steps that is proportional to the number of unknowns in a linear system of equations.
the algorithm is fast, reliable and accurate, and that the algorithm has the potential to replace the existing methods for calculating the norm of the inverse.

(1) the norm of the inverse can be estimated using the Gauss—Jordan Algorithm; (2) the estimate is obtained by maximizing the norm of the right hand side vector at each step of the Gauss-Jordan Algorithm; (3) the estimate is a good approximation of the true norm of the inverse; and (4) this algorithm is efficient in terms of the number of floating point operations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: How to calculate an estimate for the condition number for a matrix that is to be inverted by means of the Gaussian elimination algorithm.
the following problem: Given a real matrix A, how can we calculate an estimate for the norm of the inverse A−1?
the development of an algorithm for the calculation of an estimate for the condition number for the solution of a linear system of equations, by means of the classical Gauss—Jordan elimination.
